content: Digital diabetes prevention programs, such as those utilizing telehealth services and smartphone-based applications, have demonstrated significant potential in improving health outcomes for individuals at risk of developing diabetes. These technology-driven interventions can increase accessibility to preventive care and offer personalized feedback, even for individuals residing in remote or underserved areas. Furthermore, these programs are capable of delivering tailored guidance on physical activity and dietary management, which aligns with the specific needs of each individual. This personalized approach supports the adoption and maintenance of long-term lifestyle modifications essential for diabetes prevention.
